instructions.content: Run compliance checks early in development.
Prefer fixing insecure resources over suppressing findings.
Use suppressions only with explicit, reviewable rationale.
Keep CI enforcement consistent with the risk profile.
Add relevant cdk-nag rule packs to the app.
Checkpoint: if findings remain after fixing, categorize each as fix / suppress / defer before proceeding. Do not advance until every finding has an owner and decision.
Add minimal, scoped suppressions when justified.
Re-run synth and CI checks before merge.
Apply a rule pack to every stack with Aspects.of(app).add(new AwsSolutionsChecks({ verbose: true })).
Scope a suppression to the exact construct with NagSuppressions.addResourceSuppressions, not the whole stack.
NEVER suppress findings without a concrete security rationale (not 'false positive').
NEVER apply broad stack-level suppressions for convenience.
NEVER enable production rule packs only at release time; run them continuously in feature branches.
NEVER ignore recurring nag violations in CI; fix the root cause or add a justified suppression once.
Do not use this skill for Terraform-only repositories without AWS CDK constructs.
In CI, run tests and synth together (npm test && npx cdk synth) so a failure of either fails the job.
